Standardised-duration stock

Source: R/stock.R
standardized_stock.Rd

Computes the stock that the observed inflow would generate under a fixed duration distribution: S*_d = sum_j F_{d - j} G(j), where F is the daily inflow and G a survival curve from duration_survival().

Usage

standardized_stock(
  flow,
  survival,
  by = NULL,
  date_col = "date",
  flow_col = "inflow"
)

Arguments

flow

A data.frame or data.table with the daily inflow, one row per by x date.

survival

A data.table as returned by duration_survival(), with columns j, surv and optionally a subset of by.

by

Character vector of grouping columns of flow, or NULL.

date_col

Name of the date column of flow (class Date or IDate).

flow_col

Name of the inflow column of flow (non-negative, NA allowed).

Value

A data.table with columns by, date_col (IDate), stock_std (double) and complete (logical: TRUE when the day is at least max(j) days after the first date of the grid), ordered by by and date.

Details

The actual stock is S_d = sum_j F_{d - j} P_d(duration >= j) with a duration distribution that may change over time (for example when a source starts capping durations). Holding G fixed (for example at its base-period value) removes the level shifts caused by changes in the duration regime, while keeping the signal carried by the inflow. When the durations are constant and G is computed from them, S* equals the actual stock.

The flow is placed on a complete daily grid from the first to the last date over all groups; missing days count as zero inflow, while explicit NA values propagate to the max(j) + 1 days whose window contains them. The convolution is exact (one-sided, stats::filter() with zero padding before the first day). Days whose window starts before the first date of the grid are computed on a truncated window and flagged with complete = FALSE.

The survival curves are matched to the flow on the columns of by that are present in survival: a curve per source can be applied to a flow by source and skill. When survival has none of the by columns, the same curve applies to all groups.

Examples

flow <- data.table::data.table(
  date = data.table::as.IDate("2024-01-01") + 0:9,
  inflow = c(5L, 3L, 4L, 6L, 2L, 5L, 4L, 3L, 6L, 5L)
)
g <- duration_survival(
  data.table::data.table(duration = c(1L, 3L), n = c(1L, 1L))
)
standardized_stock(flow, g)
#>           date stock_std complete
#>         <IDat>     <num>   <lgcl>
#>  1: 2024-01-01       5.0    FALSE
#>  2: 2024-01-02       8.0    FALSE
#>  3: 2024-01-03       9.5    FALSE
#>  4: 2024-01-04      14.0     TRUE
#>  5: 2024-01-05      11.5     TRUE
#>  6: 2024-01-06      12.0     TRUE
#>  7: 2024-01-07      13.0     TRUE
#>  8: 2024-01-08      10.5     TRUE
#>  9: 2024-01-09      13.5     TRUE
#> 10: 2024-01-10      14.5     TRUE
